findings.attention_inference: Default attention gradients lack exact replay in these tests; strict attention passes observed replay. This is a candidate source of the earlier full-model failure, not causal proof for RTX 5090.

hardware_scope: University RTX 3070; synthetic isolated components, input gradients only.
limits: No pretrained weights, videos, optimizer, or full-model trajectory used.
Only two independent workers and two timed repetitions per policy; no statistical performance guarantee.
Strict/default policy changes are bundled; this does not isolate which flag chooses the cuDNN kernel.
3070 kernel timings do not establish the 5090 bottleneck or remaining study cost.
Default replay success for other isolated cases does not authorize disabling global determinism.
Profiler CPU/device attribution may overlap; operator rows are not additive wall time.
No operation or precision flag changed in the scientific implementation.

acceptance: Use identical synthetic FP32 values and cotangents; record all source/runtime/layout settings.
Check outputs plus input, weight, and bias gradients against the pinned Conv3d and an independent patchwise reference; declare tolerances before CUDA execution.
Require observed exact independent-process replay for each accepted candidate; preserve errors/timeouts.
Measure layout conversion, forward, backward, and memory for input-only and parameter-gradient modes.
Confirm representative RTX 5090 behavior and full-model recovery before research admission.
next_diagnostic.bounds: Retain fresh-process worker, overall wall-time, and allocator limits; no new paid rental for university comparison.
candidates: Explicit channels-last-3D input/weight layout with strict settings retained.
Explicit native backend (cuDNN disabled for isolated operation), only if deterministic support and bounds permit.
next_diagnostic.scope: Compare execution choices for the same original Conv3d before considering any equivalent replacement.
next_diagnostic.state: planned; no follow-up candidate implemented, benchmarked, or adopted
